newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta call money at 17.0/18.0 percent, no repo.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta call money at 17.0/18.0 percent, no repo.

text.p: Jakarta call money remained expensive on Friday as the central bank kept short-term rates high to contain speculative dollar buying, dealers said.
They said the central bank scrapped the offer of repo purchases and remained absent from the short-term securities (SBPUs) market to keep a tight grip on the money market.

Overnight money was traded at 17.0/18.0, slightly lower from an early high of 19.0 percent. Longer-term rates were also driven higher, with one- and three-month money quoted at 16.75/17.00 and 17.00/17.25 percent, respectively.
One local bank dealer said liquidity was a bit tight, but did not make the market suffer.

The bank offered three-day bilateral SBIs at 14.0 percent, four-to-six day at 12.0 percent, one-week at 10.0 percent, two-week at 10.5 percent, one-month at 11.125 percent, three at 11.0, six at 11.625 and one-year at 12.25 percent.
Dealers said the central bank was likely to maintain high short-term rates as the foreign exchange market continued to fluctuate with regional markets.
The average overnight interbank rate on Thursday was 18.75 percent, compared with 17.42 percent on Wednesday.
